questions.q: What is the absolute value of -12?
questions.a: The absolute value is 12. A student who answers -12 likely forgets that absolute value measures distance, which cannot be negative, and is simply stripping the bars without changing the value.

questions.q: If |x| = 5, does x have to be 5? Explain why or why not.
questions.a: No, x could be 5 or -5. A student who says "yes" does not understand that both 5 and -5 are exactly 5 units away from zero on the number line.

questions.q: A diver is at 8 metres below sea level, and a bird is flying 8 metres above sea level. Represent their distances from sea level using absolute value notation.
questions.a: The diver is at |-8| = 8 metres, and the bird is at |8| = 8 metres. A student who writes |-8| = -8 is still struggling to accept that distance is always non-negative regardless of the starting position.
|-10| is 10 and |4| is 4; therefore, |-10| > |4|. A student who thinks |-10| < |4| is comparing the original integers (-10 < 4) rather than their absolute values.

questions.q: Can the absolute value of an integer ever be negative? Justify your answer using the concept of the number line.
questions.a: No, because the absolute value measures distance from zero. Since distance is a measure of "how far" something is, it must be zero (if at the origin) or positive (if moved in any direction). A student who says "yes" is confusing the sign of the integer with the result of the absolute value function.

questions.q: Create a scenario involving money (credits and debits) where two different amounts result in the same absolute value.
questions.a: A credit of ₹50 (+50) and a debit of ₹50 (-50) both have an absolute value of 50. A poor answer would use numbers with different values, showing a failure to grasp that absolute value focuses on the magnitude of the change, not the direction (credit vs debit).
